title: The joint Destop-Desbot Wilf-equivalence conjecture for 3142, 3241, and 4132
exact_utf8_statement:
For a permutation $\tau$, let $\operatorname{Destop}(\tau)$ and $\operatorname{Desbot}(\tau)$ denote its descent top and descent bottom sets. Patterns are **$(\operatorname{Destop},\operatorname{Desbot})$-Wilf equivalent** when their avoidance classes have the same joint distribution of these two statistics for every permutation length. **The joint Destop-Desbot conjecture.** The patterns $3142$, $3241$, and $4132$ are $(\operatorname{Destop},\operatorname{Desbot})$-Wilf equivalent.
The source says this conjecture, together with the preceding classification conjectures, would identify the unique non-singleton joint equivalence class in $S_4$; the joint conjecture was verified computationally for avoiders of length at most $10$.
classification_reason: The statistics and universal distribution comparison are specified.
quantifiers: All lengths and all descent-top/bottom set pairs; equal avoidance counts for the three patterns.
technical_assessment: Needs one joint-statistic-preserving mechanism, not separate marginal Wilf equivalences; finite length checks cannot supply it.

title: The Ascbot shape-Wilf equivalence conjecture for 231⊕σ and 312⊕σ
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a nonempty permutation, let $\rho\oplus\sigma$ denote their direct sum, and let $F$ be a traversable Ferrers board. For a traversal $\tau$ of $F$, define the $F$-ascent bottom statistic $\operatorname{Ascbot}_F(\tau)$ from the ascent bottoms in its separated traversal. Two patterns are **$\operatorname{Ascbot}$-shape-Wilf equivalent** if, for every traversable board $F$, there is a bijection between their $F$-avoiders preserving $\operatorname{Ascbot}_F$. **The Ascbot shape-Wilf conjecture.** For any nonempty permutation $\sigma$, the patterns $231\oplus\sigma$ and $312\oplus\sigma$ are $\operatorname{Ascbot}$-shape-Wilf equivalent.
This claim is obtained in the source from complementing the analogous descent-top assertion; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

This extends the verified cases through $n=16$ and asks whether the observed property holds for all symmetric groups; no general proof is given in the source.

title: Inequalities between parity-separated partition functions
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal{OE}}(n)$ and $\overline{\mathcal{EO}}(n)$ denote the paper's parity-separated partition-counting functions, and let $p_0(n)$ and $p_1(n)$ be the associated partition functions. **Inequality conjecture.**

(i) For every $n\geq3$,

$$
\overline{\mathcal{OE}}(2n+1)>\overline{\mathcal{EO}}(2n).
$$

(ii) For every $n\geq1$,

$$
p_0(n)\geq p_1(n),
$$

with strict inequality unless $n\in\{1,10,13\}$. These inequalities conjecturally describe a systematic dominance between the two parity-separated partition families; the supplied text gives no resolution status beyond presenting them among the paper's conjectures.

title: Avoiding symmetrically colored 4-APs
exact_utf8_statement: A 4-AP is a progression $n,n+d,n+2d,n+3d$ with $d\neq0$. Such a coloring conjecture is posed because it would imply Ruzsa's question on Fourier-uniform 4-AP density; the paper gives a 3-coloring for $\mathbb{Z}/22\mathbb{Z}$ and proves the corresponding quantitative bound, but does not resolve the conjecture.

title: Minkowski's covering-radius conjecture for unimodular lattices

\mu(\Lambda)\leq 2^{-d}=\mu(\mathbb{Z}^d)

title: The skew corner-free set bound
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $S\subseteq[n]^2$ be **skew corner-free**, meaning that $S$ contains no three points of the form

$$
(x,y),\ (x,y+\delta),\ (x+\delta,y')
$$

with $\delta\ne0$. **The skew corner-free set conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, one has

$$
|S|\le O(n^{1+\varepsilon}).
$$

The trivial construction gives $|S|\ge n$, while Petrov's construction gives $|S|\ge\Omega(n\log n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$. The best upper bound stated here is only $O(n^2/(\log\log n)^{0.0137\cdots})$, so the conjectured near-linear bound remains open.

quantifiers: Every epsilon>0, all n and skew-corner-free S with an epsilon-dependent constant.

$$
\operatorname{ED}(X_{\bar{\mathbf{q}}, n}) = (80/3)n^3 - 368n^2 + (5068/3)n - 2580.

title: The two-orders characterization conjecture for finite simple groups
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $S$ a finite simple group. Write $\pi_e(G)$ for the set of element orders of $G$.

**Two-orders characterization conjecture.** $G\cong S$ if and only if

$$
\pi_e(G)=\pi_e(S)
$$

and

$$
|G|=|S|.
$$

Thus every finite simple group should be characterized by the order of the group and the orders of its elements. This conjecture was proposed by the author in 1987; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

title: A bound on the number of distinct prime factors of Mersenne numbers
exact_utf8_statement:

$$
\omega(N_p)<1.36\log p.
$$
 This is motivated by sieve heuristics for integers whose prime factors satisfy congruence restrictions; it would imply that only finitely many primes $p$ violate the displayed bound.

title: Existence of separating quadratic-residue tests for Mersenne factors
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $p>p_0$ be prime, assume the distinct-factor bound conjecture and the uniform-distribution conjecture, and write 
$$
2^p-1=q_1\cdots q_k,
$$

$$
\left(\frac{2^{a_i}+1}{q_j}\right)=(-1)^{\delta_{ij}}\qquad(1\le j\le k).
$$
 This would provide, for each prime factor $q_i$, an exponent whose value is a nonresidue modulo $q_i$ and a residue modulo every other prime factor; the source derives it heuristically from the preceding conjectures and an independence estimate.

title: Cyman–Dzido–Lapinskas–Lo exact conjecture for the online Ramsey number of $P_4$
exact_utf8_statement:

$$
\tilde{r}(P_4,P_n)=\left\lceil\frac{7}{5}n\right\rceil-1.

The cited work had established the lower bound $7n/5-1\leq \tilde{r}(P_4,P_n)$ and an upper bound $\tilde{r}(P_4,P_n)\leq 7n/5+9$. title: Odd Zumkeller–prime representation conjecture
exact_utf8_statement:
Let a **Zumkeller number** be a natural number whose positive divisors can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum. An odd natural number is a natural number that is not divisible by $2$.

**Odd Zumkeller–prime representation conjecture.** Every odd natural number greater than $8$ and not equal to $21$ is expressible as a sum of a Zumkeller number and a prime.

The preceding theorem shows that infinitely many even natural numbers are not expressible as a sum of a Zumkeller number and a prime. The claim is known for all odd natural numbers greater than $8$ other than those of the form $18k+3$, and has been computationally verified for $18k+3$ with $2\leq k\leq 1000$; the general case remains open.

title: Conjecture on the monotonicity of Riemann sums for reciprocal quadratics

1. $L_n(f_b)$ is neither increasing nor decreasing for all $b\in\big(\frac{1}{2},1\big)$ and is monotonically increasing for all $b\in(\beta^+,2]$.
2. $R_n(f_b)$ is neither increasing nor decreasing for all $b\in\big(1,\frac{3}{2}\big)$ and is monotonically decreasing for all $b\in(\beta^+,2)$.

The conjecture concerns the parameter ranges not covered by the preceding monotonicity theorem for left and right Riemann sums. The endpoint case $b=2$ in the first assertion is verified separately, while the remaining assertions are addressed by the paper's subsequent results.

title: Divisorial instability conjecture for blowups of Fano hypersurfaces along linear subspaces
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\Gamma \simeq \mathbb P^k \subset X$ be a $k$-dimensional linear subspace in a smooth Fano hypersurface $X \subset \mathbb P^{n+1}$ of degree $d$. Let $\varphi \colon Y \rightarrow X$ be the blowup of $X$ along $\Gamma$, and suppose that $Y$ is a Fano variety. **Divisorial instability conjecture.** There exists a constant $c(d)$ depending only on $d$ such that

$$

title: Rubinstein's Ricci iteration convergence conjecture

title: The two-term supercongruence conjecture for the original sporadic sequences
